newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher but sentiment fragile.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher but sentiment fragile.

text.p: French stocks staged a partial rebound on Friday, helped by Wall Street's late recovery, but brokers said sentiment was fragile in the French market.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 8.95 points, or 0.4 percent, at 2,265.92 at 0915 GMT, recouping only a fraction of its 2.54 percent loss on Thursday triggered by a sharp fall on the previous day in the Dow Jones industrial average.
The CAC-40 January contract was 12 points higher at 2,268.
Brokers said the market was likely to trade quietly until Wall Street's opening in the afternoon, and volume was expected to remain thin. It was just 300 million francs at 0915 GMT.
Shares in Compagnie des Salins du Midi, suspended since December 23, surged 168 francs to 608 francs, close to the 614 franc per share offer from Morton International.

Morton said on Tuesday it would buy the 50.8 percent controlling stake in Cie des Salins from Compagnie de Suez and offer the same price to minority shareholders. The bid values Cie des Salins at 1.5 billion francs.

Insurer Assurances Generales de France (AGF) was up 1.53 percent at 166.30 francs. The news magazine La Vie Francaise ran an article saying AGF may lack the critical mass to go up against the newly merged Axa-UAP entity and may become a takeover target.
